blocker_evidence.C2_GRADIENT_SEVERING_CONDITION_UNRESOLVE: REPRODUCED by C2-v3, which calls the real phase_e.run_update unmodified and substitutes only the loader. cuda+fp16 batch4/micro2: 48/48 mandatory tensors dead. cuda+fp16 batch2/micro1: 40/48 dead, survivors exactly the eight tensors of block 0. cpu, same unmodified function with autocast and GradScaler inactive, batch2/micro1: 0/48 dead. attention.output live in every condition. Zero-both-moment counts track dead counts and match the historical checkpoints. Loss falls normally (2.2177/1.9858/1.7699) while all 48 are dead. Graded with geometry and removed by dropping fp16, so this is a magnitude threshold, not a severed graph; block 5 dies while block 0 survives, so it is per-block and depth-dependent rather than sequential. Consistent mechanism: the fp32-to-fp16 cast at KernelLinearAttention.forward's 'self.output(output.to(tokens.dtype))', which every upstream tensor's gradient must cross while self.output's own gradient is taken before it. NOT yet formally isolated: the CPU control varies device, dtype and scaler together. Terminal is REPRODUCED_AND_LOCALIZED_TO_THE_FP16_PATH, not CAUSE_ESTABLISHED.

blocker_evidence.SEALED_HOLDOUT_MEMBERSHIP_PUBLICLY_READA: results/v4/stage81a2_split_registry.csv on public main discloses which donors are in the sealed_holdout split, together with the freeze seed and assignment method. NOT a privacy or PII issue: the owner confirms all donor data was obtained from already-public databases (SEA-AD is published by the Allen Institute), so donor identifiers and pathology are already in the public domain and require no remediation. The remaining issue is narrower and purely one of split concealment: a sealed holdout assumes membership is unknown until the evaluation contract is frozen, so a publicly readable membership list makes a future sealed-evaluation claim contestable regardless of whether anyone looked. Nothing to repair in git; if a sealed-holdout evaluation is proposed later, re-seal with a fresh seed and partition instead.
